title: A skydiver's fall: reaching terminal velocity
examples: Why does a skydiver stop speeding up?
How does a parachute slow you down?

explain.say: Picture a skydiver leaping out of a plane, high above the desert in Dubai. At first she speeds up fast. But a few seconds later, she stops speeding up and falls at a steady speed. Why? Let us look at the forces on her.

draw.text: A skydiver's fall: reaching terminal velocity

explain.say: Look at the arrows. Her weight, the pull of gravity, is big and points down. Air resistance, the push of air against her, points up, but it is tiny because she is slow at first. The forces are unbalanced, so she speeds up. Which arrow is bigger?

forces.label: Weight
forces.ask: Why does a skydiver speed up at first?

explain.say: Her weight, yes! Now look at the graph. The faster she falls, the harder the air pushes back. See how the line starts steep, then bends? Air resistance is growing, so she speeds up less and less each second. Is she still speeding up here?

Yes, but only a little! Look at the arrows now: air resistance has grown until it equals her weight. Balanced forces, so no more speeding up. This steady top speed is terminal velocity, about 200 kilometres per hour for a skydiver lying flat. Are the arrows equal?

Equal, perfect! Then she opens her parachute: its big area makes air resistance huge, she slows right down, and reaches a new, gentle terminal velocity. Wow fact: diving head-first, skydivers can pass 300 kilometres per hour! Challenge: why do cats survive long falls better than people?

faq.a: Terminal velocity is the steady top speed of a falling object, reached when air resistance grows to equal its weight.
asks: Why does a skydiver stop speeding up?

faq.q: Why does a skydiver speed up at first?
faq.a: At first air resistance is small, so weight is much bigger and the forces are unbalanced downwards.

faq.q: How does a parachute slow you down?
faq.a: A parachute has a large area, so it hugely increases air resistance. You slow down until the forces balance at a low speed.

faq.q: Why does air resistance increase with speed?
faq.a: The faster you move, the more air particles you hit each second and the harder they push back.

faq.q: Does a heavier object have a higher terminal velocity?
faq.a: Usually yes. More weight means air resistance must grow larger to balance it, so it needs a higher speed.

facts: A belly-down skydiver reaches a terminal velocity of about 55 m/s (about 200 km/h).
At terminal velocity, weight and air resistance are balanced, so acceleration is zero.

quiz.say: At terminal velocity, how do weight and air resistance compare?
quiz.show: At terminal velocity, how do weight and air resistance compare?
quiz.why: Balanced forces mean no acceleration, so speed stays constant.

wrong.0: Then the skydiver would still be speeding up.
wrong.1: Then the skydiver would be slowing down.

quiz.say: What happens straight after a skydiver opens the parachute?
quiz.show: What happens straight after a skydiver opens the parachute?
quiz.why: The parachute makes air resistance bigger than weight, so she decelerates to a lower terminal velocity.

wrong.1: Air resistance becomes bigger than weight, so she decelerates.
wrong.2: She keeps falling, just more slowly.
